name: Relative Clauses
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Relative Clauses module! This is how we describe people and things without starting a new sentence. In French, *Qui* and *Que* work for almost everything. In English, we have specific words for people (*Who*) and things (*Which*). The biggest challenge is translating *Dont* (Whose) and avoiding the word *What* as a connector.
contrastiveExplanation:
People vs. Things:
English: Who (People), Which (Things).
French: *Qui* acts as subject for both (L'homme qui..., Le chien qui...).

The 'What' Trap:
English: 'The book THAT I read' (Not 'The book WHAT I read').
French: *Ce que* vs *Que*. 'What' equals *Ce que*. You cannot use 'What' after a noun.

Possession (Whose):
English: The man WHOSE car is red.
French: L'homme DONT la voiture est rouge.

commonErrors.frenchConnection: Using French logic where 'Qui' applies to everything. People require 'Who'.

commonErrors.wrong: The boy that his mother is sick.
commonErrors.correct: The boy whose mother is sick.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Trying to translate 'Dont' by splitting it into 'That' + 'His'. Use 'Whose'.

commonErrors.wrong: The teacher who he is coming.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Doubling the subject. 'Who' IS the subject.

commonErrors.wrong: The house where I live in.
commonErrors.correct: The house I live in (or 'where I live').

items.questionText: This is the man ___ helped me.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Man' is a person, so we use 'Who'.

items.questionText: I lost the pen ___ you gave me.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Pen' is a thing, so we use 'Which'.

items.questionText: This is the house ___ I live.
items.feedback: Correct! 'House' is a place, so we use 'Where'.

items.questionText: Do you know the girl ___ is singing?
The car ___ is parked there is mine.
That is the school ___ I study.
I met a woman ___ speaks Chinese.
The dog ___ bit me ran away.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Dog' is an animal (thing) -> Which (or That).

items.questionText: This is the book ___ I bought.
The boy ___ is tall is my brother.
Here is the place ___ we met.
I don't like movies ___ are sad.
The teacher ___ teaches English is nice.
The bag ___ is on the table is mine.
I remember the day ___ you were born.
People ___ live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.
The bus ___ goes to the city is late.
The girl ___ is dancing is my cousin.
This is the cake ___ my mother made.
Where is the key ___ opens this door?
The boy ___ father is a doctor.
This is the man ___ car was stolen.
This is the book ___ I read yesterday.
items.feedback: Correct! You cannot use 'what' after a noun. Use 'that' or 'which'.

items.questionText: The woman ___ I met was nice.
items.feedback: Correct! When the pronoun is the Object (I met her), you can omit it. (The woman I met).

items.questionText: I don't understand ___ you said.
items.feedback: Correct! 'What' means 'The thing that'. No noun before it.

items.questionText: Do you know the reason ___ he left?
The hotel ___ we stayed was dirty.
The hotel ___ we visited was dirty.
items.feedback: Correct! We visited the hotel (Direct Object). No preposition 'in'. So we use 'Which'.

items.questionText: Everything ___ he said is true.
The person ___ you need to see is Mr. Paul.
items.feedback: Correct! Object pronoun omission. (The person [who] you need).

items.questionText: That is the girl ___ brother is famous.
Is this ___ you want?
The man ___ lives next door is loud.
The village ___ I was born is small.
The email ___ I sent you.
The friends ___ we invited didn't come.
He is the one ___ did it.
This is ___ I am talking about.
items.feedback: Correct! No noun before. 'The thing that' = What.

items.questionText: The car, ___ color is red, is fast.
items.feedback: Correct! Possession for things (Whose color = Its color) is also 'Whose'.

items.questionText: The day ___ we met was rainy.
The man to ___ I spoke.
items.feedback: Correct! After a preposition (to), you MUST use 'Whom' for people.

items.questionText: The house ___ I live.
items.feedback: Correct! Preposition + Which = Where. 'In which' is formal.

items.questionText: He passed the exam, ___ surprised everyone.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Which' refers to the whole previous sentence.

items.questionText: The woman ___ I gave the book.
The woman ___ I gave the book to.
items.feedback: Correct! If the preposition (to) is at the end, we can use 'Who' (or 'That', or nothing).

items.questionText: He has three sons, all of ___ are doctors.
I bought some apples, some of ___ were rotten.
My father, ___ is 60, is retiring.
items.feedback: Correct! Non-defining clause (with commas). You CANNOT use 'That'.

items.questionText: The reason for ___ he came is unknown.
What was the name of the man ___ car you borrowed?
This is the pen with ___ I write.
I spoke to the manager, ___ was very helpful.
Find the error: "The man who I spoke to him is here."
items.feedback: Correct! Remove 'him'. The relative pronoun replaces the object. Say 'The man I spoke to'.

items.questionText: All ___ glitters is not gold.
The company for ___ I work.
items.feedback: Correct! Company is a thing -> For which.

items.questionText: The company ___ I work for.
___ you need is love.
This is the best ___ I can do.
items.feedback: Correct! After superlatives (the best), we prefer 'that'.

items.questionText: He failed, ___ is a pity.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Which' refers to the sentence 'He failed'.

Find the error: "The car that I bought it is new."
items.feedback: Correct! Remove 'it'. The relative pronoun replaces the object. Say 'The car that I bought is new'.

items.questionText: This is all ___ I have.
The project on ___ we are working.
The project ___ we are working on.
___ you see is what you get.
The only thing ___ matters is love.
She cried, ___ made me sad.
It was John ___ called.
